universal_lens: The sovereign primitive unifies multi-scale temporal tracking via a hierarchical graph Laplacian. Nodes represent tracklets, while edges are weighted by the tensor product of appearance (cosine similarity) and spatial constraints (Euclidean field distance), forming a domain-specific affinity kernel.
gsi_mapping: GSI maps jersey confidence to a conformal prediction set over identity labels. The joint probability c(d_i d_j) acts as a likelihood ratio, updating posterior team assignments under occlusion using Bayesian filtering on broadcast telemetry.
gse_mapping: GSE utilizes field coordinates projected via homography to enforce physical state-transition priors. The absolute meter-distance edge feature strictly gates valid kinematic jumps between tracklets, pruning topologically impossible player trajectories in situational reasoning.

reasoning_traces.think:
The mathematical core of this primitive lies in constructing a robust affinity matrix W over a hierarchical graph G=(V,E), where V represents spatio-temporal tracklets. Standard Multi-Object Tracking relies heavily on continuous appearance embeddings, which suffer catastrophic failure under prolonged occlusions or uniform protective gear. Koshkina et al. introduce a dual-kernel approach: an appearance kernel utilizing FastReID cosine similarities, and a structural kernel leveraging explicit domain semantics. The jersey confidence operator c(d_i d_j) = c_1(d_i)·c_2(d_j) acts as a sparse, high-confidence prior. When the appearance manifold collapses (e.g., identical jerseys), the discrete algebraic structure of the jersey numbers provides a rigid constraint. Simultaneously, the spatial affinity kernel utilizes the absolute meter-distance |x_i - x_j| derived from CNN-based field registration. This metric enforces a physical continuity prior, penalizing edges that violate maximum plausible player velocity. The SUSHI hierarchy aggregates these local edge weights across multiple temporal scales (up to 1024 frames), allowing the Global Neural Network (MPNTrack) to resolve long-term associations. However, the derivation assumes offline processing and stable camera geometry. The breakdown regime emerges when broadcast camera zooms invalidate the pre-computed homography, causing the spatial kernel to inject noise rather than signal. Furthermore, the reliance on per-clip clustering for team IDs introduces a transductive leakage, assuming test-time statistics mirror training distributions. For GSE, the critical insight is decoupling the feature extraction (jersey OCR, homography projection) from the SUSHI hierarchy itself, applying these kernels directly to existing ByteTrack outputs.

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This work extends the classical Hungarian algorithm and Markov Random Fields used in early SORT/DeepSORT trackers. It inherits the graph-based optimization lineage of MPNTrack but injects modern computer vision priors—specifically scene text recognition (PARSeq) and deep metric learning (FastReID)—to solve the long-standing occlusion problem in sports analytics. reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: From a decision-theoretic perspective, the tracker acts as an observer attempting to infer hidden states (player identities) from noisy, partial observations. The opposing 'agent' is the environment: dynamic occlusions, camera operators executing unpredictable pans/zooms, and players intentionally masking their numbers. The model must anticipate these adversarial environmental shifts by relying on invariant features (field coordinates) when volatile features (visual crops) fail.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: A strict veto condition applies if the field registration module fails to converge on a valid homography for >20% of frames, as the spatial kernel will then dominate with erroneous distances. Additionally, if jersey OCR legibility drops below 60%, the discrete confidence product becomes a source of false positives rather than a resolving prior, mandating a fallback to pure appearance-based tracking.
